# NOTES: TWO BOOKS

## BOOK 1: PHAROS, THE EGYPTIAN (Guy Boothby, 1899, D. Appleton, NY)

**Preface:** Letter from Sir William Betford (The Grange, Bampton St. Mary, Dorset) to George Trevelyan (Lincoln's Inn Fields). Dec 14 (18--). Servant Jenkins announces visitor "Silver" (Honoré de Silva), who says he comes "from Mr. Cyril Forrester" (artist, abroad). Packet delivered; Betford writes receipt. De Silva: Forrester "has done with happiness"; "You will never see him again"; "consider him as one who is dead." Packet holds Forrester's note (to Betford and Trevelyan: publish his confession unextenuated; P.S. Matthew Simpford in the Strand keeps two of his pictures for Betford and Trevelyan) and manuscript. Betford read it 11:40 p.m. to 5:15 a.m. Six months later Trevelyan and Betford publish it.

**Forrester's narrative:**
- Ch I: Last week of March, wet night. Forrester finished Academy picture of Merenptah (Pharaoh of Exodus) with magicians. Dined with Betford and Trevelyan near Leicester Square, then theatre. Midnight at Villiers St. Drowning man cries "Help" at Cleopatra's Needle. Stranger on steps (Pharos) refuses to save him, chuckles. Forrester seizes him; Pharos described: short, small skull, broad shoulders, skin like old ivory and corpse, wrinkled, sunken eyes, fur coat, curious cap, stick, age 70+.
- Ch II: Early June, Friday. Squire George Merridew (6 ft, red face, big gold repeater watch), wife, son (Oxford, plans to enter Church), tennis-champion eldest daughter, Gwendoline, Ethel. At Academy, Forrester faints at his picture; Pharos appears with beautiful companion, Fräulein Valerie de Vocxqal (Hungarian violinist, "daughter of the gods"). Lady Medenham's (Eaton Square) musical "at home": Valerie plays her own work (dirge-like minor piece, then wild tarantella). Introduced to Pharos ("Monsieur Pharos"). Forrester feels revulsion and faintness.
- Ch III: Midnight, Forrester's studio (decorated Egyptian; mummy-case of Ptahmes, Chief of King's Magicians, under Menptah; bought by father, Egyptologist, who died). Pharos enters unseen. Reveals he has sought the mummy 15 years. Refused, Pharos hypnotises Forrester; Forrester wakes in chair at dawn.
- Ch IV: Inspector: murder at old curiosity shop (Clausand, Bonwell St.) between midnight and 1 a.m.; man seen entering alley. Forrester lies, shields Pharos. Mummy gone. Forrester visits Lady Medenham: Valerie is Pharos's ward (Hungarian noble's daughter; father killed in duel; Pharos adopted her ~7 years). Sir George Legrath (Director, Egyptian Museum, father's pupil) reveals fear of Pharos; says Pharos left for Naples. Note from Legrath: "Inquire for the man you seek from CARLO ANGELOTTI, Public Letter-writer, Theatre San Carlo, Naples."
- Ch V: Naples in summer. Angelotti (sparrow-like, white hair) now sells violins in shop reached via alley; denies knowing Pharos. Forrester sees Valerie in carriage, she gasps. Anonymous note: meet at Temple of Mercury, Pompeii, 4 p.m.
- Ch VI: Pompeii. Pharos admits he hypnotised him to get mummy; wanted it to return to tomb. Shows newspaper ("Mysterious Murder in Bonwell Street"): German Johann Schmidt confessed, shot himself at Bow Street. Forrester apologises. Pharos tours ruins (Temple of Isis, house of Tullus Agrippa; tale of Tymon the gladiator).
- Ch VII: Pharos's Naples house: art (Fra Angelico, Botticelli, Giorgione, Jan Steen). Shows Forrester's own painting; story of Baden: nobleman ruined, daughter paralysed, suicide at Kursaal. Valerie warns in drawing-room: "this place is fatal." Dinner: Pharos eats only fruit, flat cakes, and dissolved white powder in water. Monkey Pehtes. Turkish-grown cigarettes (hypnotic). Valerie plays under compulsion. Pharos proposes steam-yacht trip to Cairo; Forrester agrees. Garden-door at night: Valerie: "it would be better to die than fall into his power." Forrester vows to sail with them.
- Ch VIII: Yacht, Greek captain, ~400 tons. Pharos's cabin: plain, mummy stowed. Forrester overhears Pharos hypnotising a woman in Valerie's cabin (sandy plain, tent, sick man, "death on every hand"). Night: Pharos invoking on stern grating.
- Ch IX: Storm. Pharos cowers, "I will not die." Valerie: "it must be me."
- Ch X: Port Said, train to Cairo (Hotel, Valerie's account: fled to St Petersburg, Norway, Buda-Pesth; attempted suicide at fjord, Pharos stopped her). Night follow Pharos (carriage to Gizeh). Pyramid: Forrester lost in Queen's Chamber, screams, breakdown. Tall Arab giant (Pyramids guard). Pharos finds him, makes him drink potion before Sphinx, vision: Thebes, procession, Ptahmes (Chief Magician) disgraced—face covered. Pharos's words: "you are my property."
- Ch XI: Spot on left arm. Forrester paints the vision. Steamer to Luxor. Pharos recounts Ptahmes's history (son of Netruhôtep; Moses; plagues; Ptahmes advised Pharaoh falsely; first-born dies; Ptahmes hid, died at 50).
- Ch XII: Picture given to Pharos. Luxor: Pharos's power over locals. Salem Awad (Arab messenger). Midnight at Karnak temple: old man in white leads Forrester into hidden hall; anointed; vision of Ptahmes's rise, funeral, burial in desert tomb; mummy face = Pharos's. Old man: "Rise, Ptahmes, rise and depart!"
- Ch XIII: Forrester wakes at dawn in Hypostyle Hall; left arm swelling. Pharos returns; "Egyptian fever." Desert tent; Arab who nursed him dies. Forrester has been ill three days.
- Ch XIV: Itinerary: London June 7; Naples June 10; Cairo June 18; Luxor 27th; Constantinople; Vienna; Prague July 15 (Teyn Kirche). Forrester and Valerie confess love in Teyn Kirche; plan escape; Baumgarten park. Pharos learns love, announces Valerie will play at Emperor's concert (Franz Josef). Plague news: Constantinople, Russia, Austria, Germany.
- Ch XV: Escape Prague 6:15 a.m. to Dresden, Berlin. Dinner with Herr Schuncke (fat restaurateur). Forrester and Valerie: engaged (posing as Mr. and Miss Clifford, siblings). Wittenberge; Hamburg (Hôtel Continental). Steamboat office: no British ports open. Valerie falls ill; Pharos appears at hotel ("It is the plague"; "It is too late").
- Ch XVI: Forrester runs errands; chemists (Dittmer, drug supply) take his watch; Pharos gives opiate; Captain Wisemann (6'9", huge ears) arranges steamer "Margrave of Brandenburg." Valerie recovers. Pharos admits he watched Forrester in Berlin.
- Ch XVII: Ship; plague aboard (steward dies; Reimann; captain). Valerie refuses to land in England. Pharos: "crush you like a worm." Captain attacks Forrester; Pharos kills him by choking; swelling ("infallible sign"). England sighted at midnight.
- Ch XVIII: Landing at night; walk; Tebworth Junction station; Norwich. London: Park Lane house (formerly Lord Tollingtower's; Pharos was with him at death). Forrester's luggage from Prague already there.
- Ch XIX: Antiquarian Club dinner (Pharos eats nothing but fruit); Duchess of Amersham's ball, Carlton House Terrace; Covent Garden fancy ball; Seven Dials gambling hell (thieves). Pharos reveals a plague-infected London.
- Ch XX: Forrester learns from club map statistics that the plague spreads from the Antiquarian, ball, and fancy-ball guests. Sir George Legrath (embarrassed). Confronts Pharos: Pharos confesses: he is Ptahmes; stabbed Clausand over scarabeus; made Schmidt take blame; planted plague; "I have further need of thee. Sleep again."
- Ch XXI: Five days' hypnotic sleep. Forrester goes to Home Office; Sir Edward Grangerfield (Home Secretary) dismisses confession. Forrester gives him Hamburg prescription. Valerie finds him in St James's Park. Pharos sitting by fire in Egyptian-cluttered room, shrunken, monkey shrunken. Valerie describes a vision (hall with Paduamen, sentence). Pharos, in fit of terror, claws his throat; dies; monkey dies. Forrester collapses, brain fever. Wakes on yacht with Valerie: "Pharos is dead." THE END.

Publisher blurbs for other Boothby novels follow (Doctor Nikola, Lust of Hate, Beautiful White Devil, A Bid for Fortune, Marriage of Esther).

## BOOK 2: THE FATAL THREE (M. E. Braddon, 3 vols; Vol I: Clotho, Vol II: Lachesis, Vol III: Atropos)

### VOL I (Clotho; or Spinning the Thread)

- **Ch I:** John Fausset (stout, middle-aged, ex-silk merchant, St Paul's Churchyard and Lyons; capital withdrawn) and wife Honourable Maud Donfrey (third daughter of Lord Castle-Connell; ~28; married 9 years; 19 at marriage). Daughter Mildred (7). Home: Upper Parchment Street, off Grosvenor Sq; country house The Hook (Surrey, Thames between Chertsey and Windsor). Fausset wants to adopt orphan Fay (14; mother's name never spoken; Fausset says she is "a distant relation"). Maud: "golden circle of home-life." Mildred persuades: "Let the little girl come."
- **Ch II:** Fay arrives (tall, thin, black eyes, olive complexion, black frock). Maud: Fay "plain," "owl in an ivy-bush." Mildred gives Fay her doll; they bond. Fay given "Bell's room" (servant's room on mews, cell-like). Fay: "I hate lessons."
- **Ch III:** Mildred and Fay inseparable; Maud jealous. Martha Bell (Maud's old nurse, ~48, straight, iron-grey, black silk; husband Patrick Bell emigrated to Canada and died; she "always a power"). Bell hates Fay; Fay refuses her help. Miss Colville governess. Mildred's fine clothes vs Fay's neglected under-linen.
- **Ch IV:** Fay's past: cottage on windy hill, Nounou, sea; then school near London (Miss Constable, Streatham), expelled after temper outburst; Fausset brings her to Upper Parchment St. Summer at The Hook: Mildred catches scarlet fever; Fay nurses her. Bell and maid Meta overhear talk ("sisters"; "Mr. Fausset's guilty look"). Mildred asks mother to let her call Fay "sister"; Maud furious. Fay: "I hate everybody else in this house." Maud: "wicked, ungrateful girl." Mildred and Fay separated; Fay sent to Eastbourne-side then to finishing school in Brussels. Mildred learns via letter from Maud: "Fay is dreadfully backward... may not see her again for some years."

*(Vol I then jumps to Enderby.)*

- **Ch V:** Enderby Manor (near Romsey, Hampshire). George Greswold (married Mildred; daughter Lola, 12, golden-haired, precocious). Village fever: Johnny Giles, Mary Martin, Mrs. Peter, Mary/Polly Rainbow (only child of widow Mrs. Rainbow). Dr. Porter (village doctor). Mrs. Wadman (dairy-woman, Sunday blue merino) used polluted old garden well for dairy ~3 weeks; Dr. Hutchinson (Southampton). Greswold dismisses staff after. Bell (74) is their servant too.
- **Ch VI:** Lola falls ill (mild first, "headache"); Polly Rainbow dies; Lola dies ~10 days later. Greswold: "Judgment!" repeated at her grave (later revealed).
- **Ch VII:** Greswolds in Switzerland (Lake of Thun villa) and Vienna. George's "bad dream" (cage, iron bars). Back to Enderby. Backstory: George Ransome (second son of Squire Ransome of Mapledown, Sussex; mother left Enderby to him; took name Greswold). Brother Randolph (father's favourite); Randolph's daughters Rosalind (married Sir Henry Mountford, Rainham Hall) and Pamela (Ransome), a fox-terrier named Box. Mildred's mother Maud dies (~Mildred 16; reveals Fay was Fausset's natural daughter). Mildred's Fay memories.
- **Ch VIII:** How George met Mildred at The Hook (Mildred 17; introduced by Fausset who knew George's father at Oxford). Mildred married George at ~18; Enderby. Lola's grave: "Laura, the only child of George and Mildred Greswold, aged twelve." George: "Judgment! judgment!"
- **Ch IX:** Summer, 2 months later. Mildred uneasy. Sunday church: Mildred sees auburn-bearded stranger with "Judas face." Pamela invited to Enderby.
- **Ch X:** Stranger is Mr. Castellani (César; Milanese, guest of Riverdale). Riverdale: Tom Hillersdon (millionaire) and wife Louise Hillersdon (formerly Louise Lorraine, notorious adventuress). Castellani calls on Mildred; tells her he knew George at Nice and Lady Lochinvar's palace (implying George had a previous marriage). George goes white.
- **Ch XI:** Castellani, George's silence. Mildred suspects a secret marriage. Pamela arrives with Box.
- **Ch XII:** Castellani author of anonymous novel *Nepenthe*; arranges concert; suggests Mrs. Hillersdon and Clement Cancellor (Vicar of St Elizabeth's, Parchment Street, Mildred's old teacher).
- **Ch XIII:** Cancellor at Riverdale; Hillersdon's history; Louise's conversion; Deceased Wife's Sister's Bill debate at Enderby drawing-room (George defends marriage with a wife's sister; Cancellor condemns it).
- **Ch XIV:** Concert at Enderby (Castellani sings; Pamela sings duet). Mildred faints after seeing George's first wife's portrait: small face, large dark eyes, "Vivien Faux." George: "I have had her photograph for my days of humiliation."

### VOL II (Lachesis; or the Meter of Destiny)

- **Ch I:** Castellani's social reputation (Magnus Dudley). Concert at Enderby; Mildred collapses. Mildred goes to Queen Anne's Gate, London, to Mrs. Cecilia Tomkison (husband Adam). George's letter (grim; denies; "marriage with sister's child is not forbidden"). Mildred's letter (Fay was Fausset's daughter; mother's death-bed revelation). Cancellor: "incestuous" marriage; Mildred resolves to separate.
- **Ch II:** George questions Bell (Bell: Fay was image of Fausset; suspicions "everybody"). Vivien Faux's history: Florence; Mortimers (English artist and wife, Brussels); George met Vivien at Florence; married after brief acquaintance; her £30,000 trust (Pergament & Pergament, Lincoln's Inn Fields).
- **Ch III:** Mildred goes to Brighton. Cancellor counsels separation. Mrs. Tomkison.
- **Ch IV:** Miss Gertrude Fausset (aunt, ~57, Lewes Crescent, Brighton; St Edmund's church). Franz (Swiss butler). Miss Fausset denies knowledge of Fay's parentage. Castellani appears at evening; Mildred notices his resemblance to Fay.
- **Ch V:** George in London; Mr. Pergament refuses to name Vivien's father; Fausset's trust "under oath." Pamela goes with George to Brighton. Mildred, in husband's presence, says she must leave. Greswold: "Mildred, is it irrevocable?" He concedes; Pamela to accompany Mildred abroad. Mr. Maltravers (vicar of St. Edmund's; hopes Mildred will fund transept) and Honourable Percival Cromer (curate).
- **Ch VI:** Mildred ill (low fever). Pamela and Castellani's flirtation. Mildred plans Italy. Castellani asks to visit; Mildred and Pamela leave for Pallanza (Lago Maggiore).
- **Ch VII:** Pallanza. Castellani proposes to Mildred, is rebuffed; hints "your husband is a madman and murderer." Mildred ceases contact; Pamela unhappy.
- **Ch VIII:** Castellani's claim: George Ransome was accused of wife's murder (Vivien at St Jean, Nice, April); committed to asylum near Nice (St. André road). Mildred goes to Nice; Lady Lochinvar (Palais Montano) confirms: Vivien threw/was thrown from cliff near St Jean; George arrested; "not proven."
- **Ch IX:** Mildred visits Villa "Le Bout du Monde" (now Montfleuri) at St Jean; flower-woman guide; Dr. Leroy (asylum director) describes George's madness and recovery; George's room; Mildred prays for him. Mildred resigns herself to separation.

### VOL III (Atropos; or That Which Must Be)

- **Ch I:** Maria Castellani (singer, Paolo's cousin, madwoman in asylum; Paolo abandoned her, married a French consumptive). Dr. Leroy. Pamela at Nice courts Malcolm Stuart (Scottish, nephew of Lady Lochinvar).
- **Ch II:** George's solitude at Enderby; Pamela's letters. Backstory: George Ransome's youth; father's quarrel; travels; Florence 1866-7; met Vivien Faux (pale, dark-eyed, bitter; thinks herself nobody); married within a month. Honeymoon: Oberland, Engadine; Nice.
- **Ch III:** Vivien's jealousy at Nice; the Villa at St Jean; picnic with Delia Darcy and sister (Irish belles). Vivien's rage; on cliff path, she runs over the edge; George leaves her; she dies (April 24, 1868). Inscription: "VIVIEN RANSOME. Died April 24th, 1868. Eternally lamented."
- **Ch IV:** Inquest; George arrested; magistrate's questions; sent to asylum (Villefranche, then St André). Recovery; mother's death; George rich. Enderby.
- **Ch V:** Mildred at Nice; grave of Vivien at Villefranche hill, Mildred plants roses. Stuart courts Pamela. Mildred walks St Jean.
- **Ch VI:** Pamela's whirl; Castellani pursues again; Mildred warns Pamela; Mildred thinks Castellani scheming. Maltravers letter: Miss Fausset ill; Mildred returns to Brighton.
- **Ch VII:** Brighton; Miss Fausset declining. Mildred writes to curate Rollinson; reply: George is broken, visits daughter's grave at dusk.
- **Ch VIII:** Mildred visits Enderby churchyard; George at grave; "How should I greet thee?" Mildred leaves; rectory with Rollinson; Salisbury. Pamela engaged to Stuart; wedding planned (Westminster Abbey); Lady Lochinvar's gift; Honeymoon at The Hook.
- **Ch IX:** The Hook. Mildred searches father's cupboards; finds letters signed "M.F." from Miss Fausset (Gertrude) at Milan (1860s): affair with Paolo Castellani; sham civil marriage; brother John traced them at Vevay; child born at Evian; Fausset gave child "Fanny/Fay" to Barnes; Gertrude refused contact; settlement £30,000 India Stock (letter suggests £40,000). Mildred writes to aunt; goes back to George.
- **Ch X:** Enderby; George forgives; Mildred's heart weakens; physicians; Jenner's advice; George's fear of loss.
- **Ch XI:** Pamela's wedding in Westminster Abbey (Mr. Smithson's gown). Miss Fausset (Lewes Crescent) confesses to Mildred: loved Paolo Castellani; sham marriage; brother came; hid shame; César knew. Miss Fausset dies early winter; estate to Mildred. Mildred dies later; George dies; Greswold Hospital. Castellani survives on legacy, fading reputation. THE END.
